newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladeshis protest at new weekend.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshis protest at new weekend.

text.p: Growing protests over changes to the working week and a delay in announcing new pay scales set off clashes between Bangladesh government employees and police on Monday.

Witnesses said three protesters were injured as baton-wielding police dispersed thousands of employees calling for the restoration of the previous arrangement under which Thursday was a half-day holiday and Friday a full day.

The government last week changed the weekend to Friday and Saturday, saying it would give employees more time to take care of family matters and would reduce fuel costs for government transport. However the changes also require employees to work longer hours from Sunday through Thursday.
The move prompted workers to start daily demonstrations in Dhaka's main government secretariat, the hub of the administration.
The protesters later won the support of other workers by adding demands for the immediate announcement of new pay scales, which authorities say are in the pipeline and may almost double salaries.
The protesters accuse the government of dragging its feet over the new salaries.
"We had to act as the situation started going out of control," one police officer said on Monday, referring to the police action against the demonstrators.

Bangladesh's business community is also unhappy over the change of weekend. They wanted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to introduce weekends on Saturday and Sunday to conform with international practice.
But the government in this overwhelmingly Moslem nation refrained, apparently fearing a backlash from orthodox Islamists.
The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), led by former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, has joined forces with the protesters.
"The BNP is siding with protesters just for political reasons," one government official said on Monday.
